dayCards.quote: Supposed to meet my profs. No idea what to say.
dayCards.reply: Bank the goodwill now, before the first travel week hits.

dayCards.quote: I don't even know where the syllabus is.
dayCards.reply: Find the four things in there that actually decide your grade.

dayCards.quote: I have a system. It's just three systems.
dayCards.reply: Pick one place. Mark every exam in it.

dayCards.quote: My whole life is the team. Wouldn't know where to start.
dayCards.reply: Start one conversation outside the bubble. A name counts.

dayCards.quote: Legs are dead. Brain won't shut off.
dayCards.reply: Trade the last ten minutes of scrolling for an unload.

dayCards.quote: I don't know what's coming. That's the problem.
dayCards.reply: Run your week like film, before Wednesday runs you.

dayCards.quote: I can give you three. After that I'm lying.
dayCards.reply: Name five things you'd defend about your game.

dayCards.quote: I don't know who my advisor is. Genuinely.
dayCards.reply: Find the door and book that call.

dayCards.quote: If I set a bedtime and blow it, that's a fail.
dayCards.reply: Run one night as an experiment. You can't fail it.

dayCards.quote: Everyone's got four years of inside jokes. I've got none.
dayCards.reply: Find the one person who doesn't need the backstory.

dayCards.quote: Showing up to another team's game alone is a lot.
dayCards.reply: Bring one teammate. Two people is a crew.

dayCards.quote: Preseason didn't go the way I planned.
dayCards.reply: Replay it straight. Name what was actually in the way.

dayCards.quote: On the field I know what I bring. Off it, no idea.
dayCards.reply: Name your one skill. Find where else it already shows up.

dayCards.quote: Search what, though?
dayCards.reply: Follow one org. Let their posts find you all year.

dayCards.quote: Practice ends at 7:45, class at 8. Breakfast is theoretical.
dayCards.reply: Fix the one meal that keeps breaking. Logistics, not rules.

dayCards.quote: I think about calling home more than I call home.
dayCards.reply: Call the people who knew you before the sport did.

dayCards.quote: If it's find the number, fine. If it's feelings, I'm out.
dayCards.reply: Locate the door. Whether or not you ever need it.

dayCards.quote: My confidence is a direct feed from the depth chart.
dayCards.reply: Map where it's solid and what makes it shaky.

dayCards.quote: Baseball is the identity. That's the plan.
dayCards.reply: Build the bench behind it. Nothing's ending.

dayCards.quote: One class is getting away from me.
dayCards.reply: Re-run that syllabus before midterms decide it for you.

dayCards.quote: Game stuff, always. Backpack? Chaos.
dayCards.reply: Point the gameday ritual at a regular Monday.

dayCards.quote: It's been a month. Texting now is weird, right?
dayCards.reply: Send the text. A reply isn't required.

dayCards.quote: Career fair, mid-season, as a senior. When exactly?
dayCards.reply: Make the one move your year actually calls for.

dayCards.quote: Take my sport away and I go blank.
dayCards.reply: Build your story and goals. Then say it out loud once.

sixJobs.title: Compete like it's already happening
sixJobs.description: Confidence check-ins built for wherever your season actually is right now.
sixJobs.example: Identify one thing that's working and one thing that's getting in the way this week, not last year.
sixJobs.imageAlt: Student-athlete checking in before a game

sixJobs.title: Run your scouting report
sixJobs.description: Introduce yourself to a professor. Book the advisor meeting. Know the week before it hits you.
sixJobs.example: A syllabus review, office hours scheduled, due dates, all in one pass.
sixJobs.imageAlt: Student-athlete meeting a professor during office hours

sixJobs.title: Recruit yourself for what's next
sixJobs.description: A 30-second pitch that never mentions your sport. One message to someone whose work you're curious about.
sixJobs.example: Write it, then try it on a friend.
sixJobs.imageAlt: Student-athlete writing notes about life after sport

sixJobs.title: Build your locker room
sixJobs.description: Meet an athlete from another team. Welcome the freshman who just got here.
sixJobs.example: Revisit someone from the welcome-back event and check in for real this time.
sixJobs.imageAlt: Student-athletes from different teams talking together

sixJobs.title: Recover like it's part of training
sixJobs.description: Find your sports psych. Eat the third meal. Name the skill you give your team.
sixJobs.example: One proactive conversation about nerves or focus before you need it, not after.
sixJobs.imageAlt: Student-athlete resting and recovering after training

sixJobs.title: Sleep like it's part of training
sixJobs.description: Lay tomorrow out tonight. Swap ten minutes of scrolling for a brain-dump.
sixJobs.example: Set a realistic lights-out time for tonight only. Report back how it went.
sixJobs.imageAlt: Student-athlete laying out kit the night before

howItWorks.title: Complete quick challenges on your phone
howItWorks.description: The challenge launches September 8, and enrollment stays open through September 29. Sleep, confidence, classes, your role on the team, life after sport—Sam meets you where you are and helps you take one useful step.

howItWorks.title: Every challenge counts.
howItWorks.description: Daily participation earns your school credit toward the leaderboard.

oldWay: Talk to someone if you need it

faq.a: No. Sam is a daily conversation, not clinical care — and it'll point you to real support when something needs more than a conversation Sam can give.

faq.q: Will my coach see what I say?
faq.a: No. Private by default. You choose what, if anything, gets shared.

faq.q: What if I miss a day?
faq.a: Nothing happens. Jump back in whenever — there's no penalty and no guilt trip.

faq.q: Does my whole team have to sign up for it to count?
faq.a: No. Any American Conference student-athlete can join on their own, and every challenge still counts toward your school's total.
